e.title: EU-U.S. Insurance Dialogue Project（欧盟—美国保险对话项目）：跨境监管对话机制与逐年工作流
e.title_en: The EU-U.S. Insurance Dialogue Project: the cross-border supervisory dialogue mechanism and its year-by-year workstreams
e.title_hk: EU-U.S. Insurance Dialogue Project（歐盟—美國保險對話項目）：跨境監管對話機制與逐年工作流
e.summary: 2012 年由美国财政部联邦保险办公室（FIO）召集欧盟委员会、EIOPA 与美国各州保险监管者参与的双边监管对话项目，指导委员会下辖技术委员会逐年比较欧美监管制度；议题历经网络风险与网络保险、大数据与 AI、气候风险与韧性；EIOPA 侧另有一份 2025 年 11 月总结报告
e.summary_en: A bilateral supervisory dialogue convened in 2012 by the US Treasury Federal Insurance Office with the European Commission, EIOPA and US state insurance regulators, in which technical committees under a Steering Committee compare the EU and US regimes year by year; its topics have run from cyber risk and the cyber insurance market through big data and AI to climate risk and resilience, and EIOPA holds a further summary report dated November 2025
e.summary_hk: 2012 年由美國財政部聯邦保險辦公室（FIO）召集歐盟委員會、EIOPA 與美國各州保險監管者參與的雙邊監管對話項目，指導委員會下轄技術委員會逐年比較歐美監管制度；議題歷經網絡風險與網絡保險、大數據與 AI、氣候風險與韌性；EIOPA 側另有一份 2025 年 11 月總結報告
e.body:
**us-eu-insurance-project** 是**欧盟与美国之间的双边保险监管对话机制**（美国方面页面位于 `home.treasury.gov` 联邦保险办公室 FIO 之下）。本条目填上本词条所在站点形态普查中长期为**真空白（0）**的**「跨国监管对话」**形态。

可核实信息（**均经探活与逐字实测**）：**美国财政部页面 HTTP 200、实测 76.3KB（78,146 字节）、标题逐字为「EU-U.S. Insurance Project | U.S. Department of the Treasury」**；**其正文关键段落逐字实测**：⭐ **项目目标**——**「The objective of the Project is to increase mutual understanding and enhance cooperation between the EU and the United States in order to promote business opportunity, consumer protection, and effective supervision.」**；⭐ **起源**——**「In early 2012, FIO convened the insurance leadership of the European Commission, European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA), and state regulators to participate in a dialogue project.」**；⭐ **组织方式**——**「The Project Steering Committee oversees technical committees that analyze and compare the EU and U.S. regimes on topics of mutual interest.」**——**即**指导委员会**下辖**技术委员会**，逐年比较两套监管制度****。
**推进历程逐字实测**：**2012 年 12 月**，指导委员会发布一份双方同意的 **「Way Forward」**，**页面逐字称其「defined 7 common objectives and initiatives」**，**枚举为**：**professional secrecy/confidentiality、group supervision、solvency and capital requirements、reinsurance and collateral requirements、supervisory reporting、data collection and analysis、peer reviews、independent third party review and supervisory on-site examinations**（⚠️ **逐字写 7 项，却枚举出 8 项——本词条如实并列，不代为取舍**）；**2014 年 7 月**更新该 Way Forward 并重申承诺；**其后**公布三个新议题**（网络安全风险与网络保险市场、保险业大数据的使用、以集团内部交易为重点的集团监管后续工作）**；**2018 年**就上述议题发文并在**卢森堡**举办公开论坛；**2020 年 3 月**发布各工作组 2019 年工作的更新总结报告，**原定 2020 年 3 月的公开活动因新冠疫情推迟**；**2021 年 10 月**以线上研讨会形式举办并发布总结报告；**2022 年**指导委员会决定聚焦三个议题：**① 气候风险金融监督（含气候风险披露、监管报送与其他金融监测）② 气候风险与韧性（含创新技术、灾前减损与适应、建模）③ 技术与创新（含大数据与人工智能、把 SupTech 作为监管工具）**；**相关工作流 2022–2023 年间定期开会**；**2023 年 6 月在华盛顿州西雅图举办公开论坛**并发布三个工作流的总结报告。**页面列出并链接的报告组逐字实测**为：**2023 Public Forum（Workstream 1 Climate Risk Financial Oversight／Workstream 2 Climate Risk and Resilience／Workstream 3 Innovation and Technology）、2021 Public Forum（Cyber Insurance Market／Insurer Cybersecurity／Big Data and Artificial Intelligence）、2020 Summary**。
⭐⭐ **另一侧更近的证据（欧方）**：**本词条另经实测确认 EIOPA 侧存在一份**2025 年 11 月**的总结报告**——**该 PDF 实测 HTTP 200、337,520 字节（329.6KB）、`file` 判定为 PDF 1.7、共 9 页**；**并进一步以程序方式抽取其文本**（⚠️ **因字体编码，抽取结果丢失部分字形，故仅引用完全可辨认的句子，其余以「据该报告」转述并标注方法局限**）；⭐⭐ **其中一句完全可辨认、且是本条目最有分量的一条事实**：**「Together, the EU and US regulators oversee approximately two thirds of the global insurance market.」——欧盟与美国监管者合计监管全球保险市场约三分之二**；**另一句可辨认的表述**：**「The Steering Committee chooses key topics they consider to be fundamentally important to the protection of policyholders and financial stability.」**——**议题由指导委员会按「对保单持有人保护与金融稳定是否根本重要」选定**。

对 RIAA：**① ⭐⭐⭐ 「跨国监管对话」这一形态的难点在于它通常**不是一家机构，而是一套机制****——**这正是本站普查此前一直把它读成 0 的原因（按机构名检索天然打不出命中）**；**本条目首次把它落成两条可核实的一手页面（美方 Treasury ＋ 欧方 EIOPA），从而说明该形态**确实存在且持续运作到 2025 年 11 月****（**⚠️ 但这不等于「本站已覆盖跨境监管对话」——本条目覆盖的是**这一对**（欧美）的**一个**项目**）。**② ⭐⭐⭐ 「约三分之二的全球保险市场」是对读者最有用的一条量化事实**——**它一句话讲清「为什么这两个辖区的对话重要」**；**⚠️ 该句出自 EIOPA 2025 年 11 月报告、系**程序抽取**所得（**字形丢失已如实说明**），**故词条内标注为「据该报告」，不主张已核实其统计口径与计算基础**；**可与池内 [[iais]] 的全球监管框架、[[insurance-europe]] 的欧洲行业立场、[[geneva-association]] 的全球风险研究并读**：**三者分别是全球规则、区域行业与全球研究，而本条目是**两个辖区之间的对等对话机制****。**③ ⭐⭐ 「议题按『对保单持有人保护与金融稳定是否根本重要』选定」是一条可直接引用的**机制设计说明****——**它把「为什么谈这些而不谈那些」写成选择标准，而非一份无从追问的议题清单**（可与 [[iais-icp]]、[[iais-gimar]] 并读）。**④ ⭐⭐ 议题演变本身就是一份**监管关切时间线**，且对精算学生有直接价值**：**网络风险与网络保险 → 大数据与 AI → 气候风险金融监督与气候韧性 → AI 与 SupTech 作为监管工具**——**2022 年起把「气候」与「技术与创新」并列为两条主线，说明二者已从专题升为长期工作流**；**可与 [[ngfs]]、[[dfa-climate-datasets]]、[[climate-conditioned-cat]]、[[naic-ai-oversight]]、[[continuous-monitoring-ai-risk]] 并读**（**未打开任何一份总结报告正文，故不转述其结论**）。**⑤ ⭐⭐ 「2020 年 3 月的公开活动因新冠疫情推迟」值得单独记一笔**——**这是一条罕见的、把**机制自身受外部冲击**写进记录的例子**；**对研究监管协作连续性的人，这类「中断与恢复」记录比顺利年份更有信息量**（**2020 年推迟 → 2021 年改线上**）。**⑥ ⚠️ 一处必须指出的**页面时效问题****：**美国财政部页面在叙述 2017–2019 年议题时仍以「Most recently（最近）」开头，**而其后内容已推进到 2023 年**——**页面措辞未随内容更新**；**且该页本次未见 2024 年以后的记录，而 EIOPA 侧已有 2025 年 11 月报告**——**故本词条**不**以 Treasury 页面的截至范围代表项目现状**，**也不主张该项目 2024–2025 年间的具体安排**。

⚠️ **如实标注**：**①** 本次核实的是**美国财政部该页面的 HTTP 状态、体量、标题与正文关键段落（逐字）**，**以及 EIOPA 侧一份 PDF 的 HTTP 状态、字节数、PDF 版本与页数，并对其文本做了程序化抽取**——⭐ **但**未打开该页面链接的任何一份总结报告**（2023 三份、2021 三份、2020 总结均未打开）**，**未访问欧盟委员会或 EIOPA 的项目主页，未访问任何一次公开论坛的材料**，因此**不能转述任何一次对话的结论、比较结果、共识或分歧**；**② ⚠️⚠️ 对 EIOPA 2025 年 11 月报告的**方法局限已写明**：**文本系程序抽取、因字体编码丢失部分字形**，**故只引用完全可辨认的句子，其余以「据该报告」转述**；**「约三分之二」未核实其统计口径、年份与来源**；**③ ⭐ **未核实**该 PDF 的正式标题、发布日期字段与发布主体署名**——**「2025 年 11 月」来自抽取文本首部字样与检索结果标题，本词条据此标注，不主张已从文件元数据独立确认**（**该 PDF 实测无 `/Title` 元数据**）；**④ ⭐ 「7 项」与枚举出的 8 项不一致，**本词条如实并列、不代为解释**——**可能是笔误、也可能某项被合并计为一项**，**本次未追查 Way Forward 原文**；**⑤ 该项目是否仍在运作、2024 年以后是否继续开会本次未核实**（**仅知欧方存在 2025 年 11 月报告**）；**⑥ 该机制是否具法律效力、其产出对成员国是否具约束力本次未核实**——**本词条**不主张**其结论具有约束力或已被任何辖区采纳**；**⑦ 中欧、港美或其他区域的同类机制本次未检索**，**故**不主张**「跨国监管对话」这一形态已被完整覆盖**；**⑧ 是否有中文材料本次未核实**。**核实说明**：财政部页面经 `discovery/probe-urls.sh` HTTP 200 实测（76.3KB／78,146 字节），正文经 HTML 文本化后逐字读取；EIOPA PDF 经探活实测 HTTP 200（337,520 字节、PDF 1.7、9 页），文本经程序抽取（**字形有丢失**）；**未打开任何一份总结报告，未访问欧盟委员会或 EIOPA 项目主页**。
e.body_en:
**us-eu-insurance-project** is **the bilateral insurance supervisory dialogue mechanism between the European Union and the United States** (the US-side page sits under the Federal Insurance Office at `home.treasury.gov`). This entry fills the **"cross-border supervisory dialogue"** form, which had long read as a **true zero** in this site’s census.

Verifiable details (**all measured by probing and read verbatim**): the **US Treasury page returned HTTP 200, measured 76.3KB (78,146 bytes), with the title verbatim "EU-U.S. Insurance Project | U.S. Department of the Treasury"**; **key passages read verbatim**: ⭐ **the objective** — **"The objective of the Project is to increase mutual understanding and enhance cooperation between the EU and the United States in order to promote business opportunity, consumer protection, and effective supervision."**; ⭐ **the origin** — **"In early 2012, FIO convened the insurance leadership of the European Commission, European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA), and state regulators to participate in a dialogue project."**; ⭐ **the structure** — **"The Project Steering Committee oversees technical committees that analyze and compare the EU and U.S. regimes on topics of mutual interest."** — **a Steering Committee over technical committees comparing the two regimes year by year**.
**Progress read verbatim**: in **December 2012** the Steering Committee published an agreed **"Way Forward"**, which the page says verbatim **"defined 7 common objectives and initiatives"**, **enumerating**: professional secrecy/confidentiality, group supervision, solvency and capital requirements, reinsurance and collateral requirements, supervisory reporting, data collection and analysis, peer reviews, and independent third party review and supervisory on-site examinations (**⚠️ the text says 7 but enumerates 8 — recorded as found, not reconciled here**); in **July 2014** the Way Forward was updated and the commitment reaffirmed; **next** three new initiatives were announced (**cybersecurity risk and the cyber insurance market, the use of big data in the insurance sector, and continuation of group supervision work focused on intra-group transactions**); in **2018** papers were published on those topics and a public forum was held in **Luxembourg**; in **March 2020** updated summary reports on the working groups’ 2019 work were published and **the public event scheduled for March 2020 was postponed because of COVID-19**; in **October 2021** a public virtual webinar was held with summary reports; in **2022** the Steering Committee decided to focus on three topics: **① climate risk financial oversight (including climate risk disclosures, supervisory reporting and other financial surveillance) ② climate risk and resilience (including innovative technology, pre-disaster mitigation and adaptation, and modelling) ③ technology and innovation (including big data and AI, and SupTech as a regulatory tool)**; the **workstreams met regularly in 2022-2023**; and in **June 2023 a public forum was held in Seattle, Washington**, with summary reports for the three workstreams. **The report groups listed and linked on the page, read verbatim**, are: **2023 Public Forum (Workstream 1 Climate Risk Financial Oversight / Workstream 2 Climate Risk and Resilience / Workstream 3 Innovation and Technology), 2021 Public Forum (Cyber Insurance Market / Insurer Cybersecurity / Big Data and Artificial Intelligence), and 2020 Summary**.
⭐⭐ **Closer evidence from the other side (the EU)**: this entry also **measurably confirmed a summary report dated November 2025 on EIOPA’s side** — the PDF **measured HTTP 200, 337,520 bytes (329.6KB), identified by `file` as PDF 1.7, 9 pages**; **its text was further extracted programmatically** (⚠️ **font encoding dropped some glyphs, so only fully legible sentences are quoted and the rest is reported as "according to that report" with the method limitation stated**); ⭐⭐ **one fully legible sentence is the entry’s weightiest fact**: **"Together, the EU and US regulators oversee approximately two thirds of the global insurance market."**; **another legible statement**: **"The Steering Committee chooses key topics they consider to be fundamentally important to the protection of policyholders and financial stability."**

For RIAA: **① ⭐⭐⭐ The difficulty of the "cross-border supervisory dialogue" form is that it is usually **not an institution but a mechanism**** — **exactly why this site’s census had long read it as zero (searching by institution name naturally returns nothing)**; **this entry is the first to ground the form in two verifiable first-party pages (US Treasury and EU EIOPA), showing the form exists and ran at least to November 2025** (**⚠️ which is not the same as "cross-border dialogue is covered" — this covers one project between one pair, the EU and US**). **② ⭐⭐⭐ "Approximately two thirds of the global insurance market" is the most useful quantitative fact here** — **it explains in one sentence why dialogue between these two jurisdictions matters**; **⚠️ it comes from the EIOPA November 2025 report and was obtained by programmatic extraction (the glyph loss is stated)**, **so the entry attributes it to that report and does not claim to have verified its statistical basis or reference year**; **readable with [[iais]] (the global regulatory framework), [[insurance-europe]] (the European industry position) and [[geneva-association]] (global risk research)** — **global rules, a regional industry voice and global research, versus a peer-to-peer dialogue between two jurisdictions**. **③ ⭐⭐ The line that topics are chosen by the Steering Committee for being "fundamentally important to the protection of policyholders and financial stability" is a directly citable mechanism-design statement** — **it turns "why these topics and not others" into a stated criterion rather than an unanswerable topic list** (**readable with [[iais-icp]] and [[iais-gimar]]**). **④ ⭐⭐ The topic sequence is itself a timeline of supervisory concern, and it is directly useful to actuarial students**: **cyber risk and cyber insurance → big data and AI → climate risk financial oversight and climate resilience → AI and SupTech as a regulatory tool** — **from 2022, climate and technology/innovation sit as two parallel main lines, showing both moved from special topics to long-term workstreams**; **readable with [[ngfs]], [[dfa-climate-datasets]], [[climate-conditioned-cat]], [[naic-ai-oversight]] and [[continuous-monitoring-ai-risk]]** (**no summary report body was opened, so none of their conclusions are restated**). **⑤ ⭐⭐ That the March 2020 public event was postponed by COVID-19 deserves separate note** — **a rare case of a mechanism recording its own interruption by an external shock**; **for anyone studying the continuity of supervisory cooperation, such interruption-and-resumption records carry more information than smooth years** (**postponed in 2020, moved online in 2021**). **⑥ ⚠️ One page-currency problem must be flagged**: **the US Treasury page still opens its 2017-2019 topic passage with "Most recently", while the content that follows runs to 2023** — **the wording was not updated with the content**; **and the page shows no record beyond 2023 while EIOPA already has a November 2025 report** — **so the entry does not treat the Treasury page’s cut-off as the project’s present state, nor claim its 2024-2025 arrangements**.

⚠️ **Stated plainly**: **①** this check verified **the US Treasury page’s HTTP status, size, title and key verbatim passages**, **plus one EIOPA PDF’s HTTP status, byte count, PDF version and page count with its text programmatically extracted** — ⭐ **but opened none of the summary reports linked from that page (three 2023 reports, three 2021 reports and the 2020 summary), did not visit the European Commission’s or EIOPA’s project pages, and did not visit any public forum material**, so **no dialogue conclusion, comparison result, consensus or disagreement can be restated**; **② ⚠️⚠️ The method limitation for the EIOPA November 2025 report is stated**: **the text was programmatically extracted and lost glyphs to font encoding**, **so only fully legible sentences are quoted and the rest is reported as "according to that report"**; **the "two thirds" figure’s statistical basis, reference year and source were not verified**; **③ ⭐ The PDF’s formal title, publication date field and issuing-body attribution were not verified** — **"November 2025" comes from the extracted text header and the search result title, and the entry labels it as such without claiming independent confirmation from file metadata** (**the PDF measurably has no `/Title` metadata**); **④ ⭐ The "7 objectives" versus eight enumerated items is recorded side by side and not reconciled** — **it could be a page error, or an item counted as one**; **the Way Forward original was not traced**; **⑤ whether the project is still running and whether meetings continued after 2024 were not verified** (**only that a November 2025 report exists on the EU side**); **⑥ whether the mechanism has any legal force, and whether its outputs bind member states, were not verified** — **the entry does not claim its conclusions are binding or have been adopted anywhere**; **⑦ comparable mechanisms involving China-EU, Hong Kong-US or other regions were not searched**, **so the entry does not claim the "cross-border supervisory dialogue" form is fully covered**; **⑧ whether Chinese-language material exists was not verified**. **Verification note**: the Treasury page was probed at HTTP 200 (76.3KB / 78,146 bytes) with the body read verbatim after HTML text conversion; the EIOPA PDF was probed at HTTP 200 (337,520 bytes, PDF 1.7, 9 pages) with text extracted programmatically (**glyph loss stated**); **no summary report was opened and neither the European Commission’s nor EIOPA’s project page was visited**.
e.body_hk:
**us-eu-insurance-project** 是**歐盟與美國之間的雙邊保險監管對話機制**（美國方面頁面位於 `home.treasury.gov` 聯邦保險辦公室 FIO 之下）。本條目填上本站形態普查中長期為**真空白（0）**的**「跨國監管對話」**形態。

可核實資訊（**均經探活與逐字實測**）：**美國財政部頁面 HTTP 200、實測 76.3KB（78,146 位元組）、標題逐字「EU-U.S. Insurance Project | U.S. Department of the Treasury」**；⭐ **項目目標逐字**：**「The objective of the Project is to increase mutual understanding and enhance cooperation between the EU and the United States in order to promote business opportunity, consumer protection, and effective supervision.」**；⭐ **起源逐字**：**「In early 2012, FIO convened the insurance leadership of the European Commission, European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA), and state regulators to participate in a dialogue project.」**；⭐ **組織方式逐字**：**「The Project Steering Committee oversees technical committees that analyze and compare the EU and U.S. regimes on topics of mutual interest.」**。
**推進歷程逐字實測**：**2012 年 12 月**發布 **「Way Forward」**，**頁面逐字稱「defined 7 common objectives and initiatives」並枚舉 8 項**（⚠️ **寫 7 卻列 8，如實並列不代為取捨**）；**2014 年 7 月**更新；**其後**公布三個新議題（網絡安全風險與網絡保險市場、保險業大數據、以集團內部交易為重點的集團監管）；**2018 年**發文並在**盧森堡**舉辦公開口論壇；**2020 年 3 月**發布更新總結報告，**原定 2020 年 3 月的公開活動因新冠疫情推遲**；**2021 年 10 月**改線上並發布總結報告；**2022 年**聚焦三議題：**①氣候風險金融監督 ②氣候風險與韌性 ③技術與創新（含大數據與人工智能、以 SupTech 作監管工具）**；**2022–2023 工作流定期開會**；**2023 年 6 月在西雅圖舉辦公開口論壇**。
⭐⭐ **歐方更近的證據**：**實測確認 EIOPA 側存在一份**2025 年 11 月**總結報告**——**HTTP 200、337,520 位元組（329.6KB）、`file` 判定 PDF 1.7、共 9 頁**；**並程序化抽取其文本**（⚠️ **因字體編碼丟失部分字形，只引用完全可辨認的句子**）；⭐⭐ **其中完全可辨認、最有分量的一句**：**「Together, the EU and US regulators oversee approximately two thirds of the global insurance market.」——歐美監管者合計監管全球保險市場約三分之二**；**另一句**：**「The Steering Committee chooses key topics they consider to be fundamentally important to the protection of policyholders and financial stability.」**

對 RIAA：**① ⭐⭐⭐ 該形態的難點在於它通常**不是一家機構，而是一套機制****——**這正是本站普查此前一直讀成 0 的原因**；**本條目首次把它落成美方 Treasury ＋ 歐方 EIOPA 兩條一手頁面**（**⚠️ 但不等於「已覆蓋跨國監管對話」——本條目只覆蓋歐美這一對的一個項目**）。**② ⭐⭐⭐ 「約三分之二的全球保險市場」是對讀者最有用的一條量化事實**（**⚠️ 出自 EIOPA 2025 年 11 月報告、系程序抽取所得，字形丟失已如實說明；不主張已核實其統計口徑**）；可與 [[iais]]、[[insurance-europe]]、[[geneva-association]] 並讀——**三者分別是全球規則、區域行業與全球研究，本條目是**兩個轄區之間的對等對話機制****。**③ ⭐⭐ 「議題按『對保單持有人保護與金融穩定是否根本重要』選定」是可直接引用的**機制設計說明****（可與 [[iais-icp]]、[[iais-gimar]] 並讀）。**④ ⭐⭐ 議題演變本身就是一份**監管關切時間線****：**網絡風險→大數據與 AI→氣候風險與韌性→AI 與 SupTech**（可與 [[ngfs]]、[[dfa-climate-datasets]]、[[climate-conditioned-cat]]、[[naic-ai-oversight]]、[[continuous-monitoring-ai-risk]] 並讀）。**⑤ ⭐⭐ 「2020 年 3 月公開活動因疫情推遲」值得單獨記一筆**——**把**機制自身受外部衝擊**寫進記錄**。**⑥ ⚠️ 必須指出的**頁面時效問題****：**敘述 2017–2019 議題時仍以「Most recently」開頭，而其後內容已推進到 2023 年**；**該頁未見 2024 年以後記錄，而歐方已有 2025 年 11 月報告**。
